### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 51 pages)`, `os validate (command, 92 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `064d8c5c1767ad02fd4974b68e6fdc2e6e2928f9` — the merge of head `d04836d59af212b7ed07c5f3f50949f15c468212` into base `4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 064d8c5c1767ad02fd4974b68e6fdc2e6e2928f9 && git checkout 064d8c5c1767ad02fd4974b68e6fdc2e6e2928f9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 d04836d59af212b7ed07c5f3f50949f15c468212 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 && git merge --no-ff d04836d59af212b7ed07c5f3f50949f15c468212

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · REWORK (one declaration line)** · Head-sha: `528e8c162b401a1e20bcb6114d00d16a4b45b4aa` · card #34726 (`Fixes #34726`) · read 2026-11-18T09:44Z

Net diff against merge base `a6cf988eb3`: 16 files, +715 / -20. Not governed. The order is claim 6971821177 as corrected by Premise corrected 6972083658 (route A: CLI only, no lint or spec change). CI was still running at this read: no job had failed yet, and Test Core, Build Core and several lint lanes were in progress. The fix below moves the head anyway, so I re-check gates at the new head.

### Must fix

- **M1. The changeset and the PR body must declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, not `Clause-②: no`.** This answers the dev's own question.
  - `os verify --json` is a documented machine face. `deployment/cli.mdx` lists its report keys, and this PR adds `capabilities` to that list. A new key in a documented CLI `--json` document is an additive change to a published contract.
  - This repository has declared it that way before, in `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md`:
    - `os verify --dashboard-windows`, whose `--json` gains `dashboardWindows`: `Clause-②: yes`.
    - `os migrate plan`, whose `--json` gains a `schemaSyncIndexes` entry: "Clause-②: yes (widening) — additive CLI …".
  - Nothing accepted before is refused, so the arm is `(widening)`.
  - Keep `Metadata-protocol: none`, because what an author can write is unchanged. Keep the level at `patch`, because AGENTS.md says a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`.
  - Consequence: with `Clause-②: yes`, the PR owes L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT` (contract-review.md, "仅凭 `Clause-②: yes` 申报而欠").
  - The new `os validate --json` / `os build` warnings entries and `os serve`'s start-up line keep their existing shapes, so they add nothing further to this.

### Should fix (seat-side)

- **S1. The wiring heuristic's false negative has no carrier.** Any class `@objectstack/security-enterprise` exports counts as wired, so `AiSeatPlugin` alone silences the `hierarchy-security` warning. The dev report lists this as "carrier: none". The tightening needs a per-token plugin identity on the registry row, which is a spec field. File it as a card, or record on #34726 why it is not worth one.
- **S2. File the exit-code parity question before landing.** For the 6 cloud tokens, `os validate` exits 1 while `os verify` reports `validate: 'error'` and exits 0. The PR says the seat files this; it is not yet filed.

### Checked, holds

- **Against the card's acceptance, as corrected.**
  - (1) The integration test spawns the source CLI against an open-edition stack with `requires: ['hierarchy-security']` and a `unit_and_below` grant. The same sentence appears in `os validate --json` `warnings` and in `os verify --json` `capabilities`. The wired control gets nothing from either. Ablation B (dropping `capabilities`) turned both cases red.
  - (2) The unit battery is derived from `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS`: one pair per non-`open` token, 7 today, with a floor. Ablation A (wiring forced to "wired") turned 4 cases red.
  - (3) "The skills and docs … say which edition enforces them": this PR covers the docs, and the skills half already holds on main. `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` L414-419 says the hierarchy-relative three "need the paid `@objectstack/security-enterprise` plugin, **fail closed to `own`** without it". So `Fixes` is right, and the dev's skills follow-up (verify's new field) is optional.
  - The card's literal case (a scope with nothing declared) is already refused by `defineStack` and the save door, as the premise correction measured.
- **Registry-driven.** Which tokens get a finding comes only from the `edition` tag. `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_CONSEQUENCE` only sharpens the sentence, and a test pins each of its keys to an enterprise registry row. There is no edition upsell wording, as triage asked.
- **`preflightProviderWiring`.**
  - It considers only tokens with `status: 'ok'`, `edition: 'enterprise'` and a package. It looks up the verdict once per package.
  - A string `plugins[]` entry naming the package counts as wired without loading it. Otherwise it loads the module through `serve`'s host importer and matches exported function names with `providesCapability`, the identity rule `serve` uses.
  - A load failure is reported as `unloadable`, never read as wired.
  - Top-level `requires` takes precedence over package bodies, the same rule as `preflightDeclaredCapabilities`.
  - It is wired into `validate.ts` and `compile.ts`, which the closed gate-parity ledger requires, and into verify through `judgeDeclaredCapabilities`.
- **`os verify`.**
  - `runCapabilityAdvisories` runs after `runAuthorTimeStage`, so a refused stack still exits there, unchanged.
  - Errors map to `validate: 'error'` and warnings to `'warning'`. The text face suffixes the error case with "`os validate` refuses this stack.".
  - The exit code reads only `hardFailures`, which is unchanged.
- **`os serve`.**
  - The start-up line covers only declared tokens with no resolver row, no tier block, and membership in `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS`. It is a warning, the boot is unchanged, and the runtime still fails closed.
  - I checked the cloud repository's app configs (`apps/*/objectstack.config.ts`). The only one that declares `hierarchy-security` is `ee-authz-showcase`, which has `plugins: [new SecurityEnterprisePlugin()]`, so it prints nothing. No cloud host declares a cloud-tier token at top level.
- **Docs, read sentence by sentence.**
  - `permission-sets.mdx`'s new paragraph matches the code: the token is declared, the plugin is wired into `plugins[]`, and validate, verify (`capabilities`) and serve each name it.
  - The `index`, `permissions-matrix`, `positions` and `administrator-guide` lines all say enterprise-enforced and owner-only on the open edition. "The three hierarchy scopes in between" is correct, since `own` and `org` are open.
  - `cli.mdx` takes the capability-provider check out of the "stays `os validate`'s" list, adds the advisory paragraph (exit status never changed, cloud tokens included), and adds `capabilities` to the report keys with its three fields and `[]`.
- **Changeset** (this PR's own file, `@objectstack/cli` patch), read sentence by sentence. All four bullets hold against the diff. M1 is the only change it needs. No `content/docs/releases/` path is touched, and no changeset already on main is edited.
- **Merges** cleanly. Main's base is `a6cf988eb3`, which already includes the merged #34791 that the claim named as a serial constraint.

### Nits (no change asked)

- `serve.ts`'s comment says the line prints "only when nothing in `plugins[]` provides it". That holds for `enterprise` tokens. A cloud-tier token is printed whatever `plugins[]` holds, the same as `os validate` refuses it whatever `plugins[]` holds.
- `os validate` and `os build` now import the provider package for a declared, resolvable enterprise token, so the module's top-level code runs at build time. The PR's Acceptance notes say this.

### Still owed

- M1 at a new head, then my delta re-read, with gates read green at that head.
- L2 at `TIER_DEFAULT`, which the `Clause-②: yes` declaration triggers.

Its first lines are `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, the same pair as the PR body. - **The changeset does not match what the diff publishes on one axis: M1.** This repository's precedents for a new `os validate --strict` failure both say so in the changeset. In `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` at this head, entry 7a1faf1 has a "What a CI job sees: `objectstack validate --strict` … now exit 1" paragraph (L13639), declared `yes (widening)` (L13641). The per-package rule entry carries "**BREAKING** — `os validate --strict` can now fail a project it passed before" (L14975). This changeset has neither.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d04836d59af212b7ed07c5f3f50949f15c468212`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. This is a delta record over the FAIL record 6975671274 at `18ce97f82ac3ac7d6f9c1d3ffbd5ec2eb2c867b0`. The PR body and the changeset both declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The 16-file list has no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path.

Inputs:
- card #34726: its body and all 8 comments, including os-dev-report 6976004319 (fix round 2);
- PR #35168: its body as it reads now, its 6 comments (FAIL 6975671274, L1 delta 6975661070, review claim 6976041264) and its file list;
- the delta `18ce97f8..d04836d5`: 1 file, +1 line, `.changeset/34726-enterprise-capability-advisory.md` only;
- the net diff from merge base `a6cf988eb3` to the head: 16 files, +716 / -20;
- the head's check-runs.

I used read-only git on the fetched head. Nothing was checked out, built or run.

**What stands.** The delta touches no code, test or doc file. Every judgment in 6975671274 that is not M1 stands unchanged and is not repeated here: ① for `os verify` (`capabilities`, exit status, text face), for the default faces of `os validate` and `os build`, for the remedy text, `os serve`, the TypeScript surface, the dependencies and the spec; ② for the level; ③ for the dev flags, N1, N2, SQL push-down and the author.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The `os validate --strict` exit-1 path is now declared. Right.** The new changeset bullet says that `os validate --strict` and `os validate --json --strict` now exit 1 for a stack whose `enterprise` capability package resolves but is not wired into `plugins[]`, or resolves but fails to load. It also says that without `--strict`, and in `os build`, the exit status is unchanged. I checked this against the code at this head:
  - `validate.ts` L1045-1054: `preflightProviderWiring` findings, in both states `unwired` and `unloadable`, are folded into `capProviderWarnings`.
  - L1315-1316: those warnings are pushed onto `warnings`.
  - L1369: `strictFailing = warnings.length - infoFindings`. Only registry `info` findings are excluded, so the capability warnings count.
  - Both faces gate on `strictFailing`: the JSON face through the exit-code argument at L1440, and the text face at L1476.
  - `capability-preflight.ts`: `preflightProviderWiring` reaches its judgment only for a token with `status: 'ok'` (its package resolves), `edition: 'enterprise'` and a provider package. `unloadable` is the case where the loader throws for such a package. So "resolves but is not wired" and "resolves but fails to load" are exactly the two `wiring` states.
  - Before this PR such a stack raised no capability warning, because an `ok` status produced none. Its `--strict` exit was therefore 0, as the bullet implies.
- **`os build` is unchanged. Right.** Its flags at this head (`compile.ts` L113 onward) are `output`, `json`, `strict-body`, `runtime-bundle`, `no-runtime-bundle` and `update-access-matrix`.
